analysis:
Documentation-only PR. Changed lines in docs/provider/cli-reference.md: the last-updated date bump (line 3), a schema-5 benchmark note (head ~583-588), and a new env-var table row at head line 1755 listing DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS as scheduler tunables. docs/reference/configuration.md (line 393-395) replaces the solo-prefill stripe row with the prefill-chunk row. Its patch excerpt is truncated and no head text unit was supplied, so I could not read the full wording.

The new row sits in the table of variables read by the engine. The surrounding text at lines 1699-1705 says that only variables in LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys and inferencePassthroughEnvKeys are copied into the provider plist, and that the rest reach the engine only under --foreground or --local. The doc does not say whether the two new keys are forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The table is a mixed list, since other entries like DARKBLOOM_CBV2_MAX_PARTIAL_PREFILLS are also present. Whether the two new keys are actually forwarded or are foreground-only is therefore unverified. It is an implementation question for the code in LaunchAgent.swift and EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift, which were not supplied.

No security controls, trust boundaries, attestation, authorization, encryption or prefix-cache storage behavior (T-041) are altered. The docs describe scheduler geometry and benchmark reporting only. The benchmark change is a local diagnostic that does not touch coordinator or consumer data paths. Scheduler geometry tunables could affect availability (T-010, T-029) or memory admission, but that depends on the code behavior rather than the docs, and the doc text shows no regression.

No findings. A later pass that sees the source should confirm the bounds on the new prefill-chunk and step-token environment variables and whether they are forwarded to the daemon.
